questions.q: In SOQL, when should a string literal be wrapped in quotes in a WHERE clause?
options: Only when the string contains spaces
Always — string literals take single quotes, while numbers and booleans don't
Never — SOQL does not use quotes around literals
Only inside aggregate functions
questions.explain: String literals like 'Technology' always need single quotes; numeric and boolean literals such as 1000000 or true do not.

questions.q: WHERE Industry = 'Technology' AND AnnualRevenue > 1000000 returns which accounts?
options: Accounts matching either condition
Every Technology account, regardless of revenue
Every account with revenue over 1,000,000, regardless of industry
Only accounts that are Technology industry AND have revenue over 1,000,000
questions.explain: AND requires both conditions to be true for a row to be returned — only Technology accounts over the revenue threshold qualify.

questions.q: Why do mixed AND/OR conditions in a WHERE clause need parentheses?
options: Without them, SOQL evaluates AND before OR, which can produce a different result than intended
Parentheses are required by SOQL syntax even with only one condition
OR is not supported in SOQL without parentheses
Parentheses convert the WHERE clause into a subquery
questions.explain: Operator precedence evaluates AND before OR; parentheses make the intended grouping explicit and prevent an unintended result set.

questions.q: If a user's profile denies field-level security read access to a field, what happens when a query requests that field?
options: The field returns as an empty string
The query throws a compile error
The field is not returned, even though it was named in the query
Field-level security is ignored by SOQL
questions.explain: Field-level security is enforced independently of the query itself — a field the user can't read is withheld, not returned empty or in error.

questions.q: What is true about sharing rules and a WHERE clause?
options: A WHERE clause can be written to bypass sharing rules for a specific record
A WHERE clause narrows rows among those a user is already allowed to see; it never grants additional access
Sharing rules only apply to reports, not to SOQL queries
WHERE clauses automatically disable sharing rules for that query
questions.explain: Sharing and WHERE operate independently — sharing decides what's visible at all, and WHERE further filters within that visible set.
